holidays.name: Science Fiction Day
holidays.description: Fans of robots, rocket ships, time machines and tentacled aliens get a day to geek out. Re-read a classic, binge a space saga, or debate whether warp drive is more plausible than time travel.
holidays.origin: The day is observed on January 2 because it is widely linked to the birthday of author Isaac Asimov, who is commonly given as January 2, 1920. It is an unofficial observance rather than a government-recognized holiday.
holidays.funFact: Isaac Asimov wrote or edited hundreds of books, and his Three Laws of Robotics have shaped how both writers and engineers talk about artificial intelligence.

holidays.name: Run It Up the Flagpole and See If Anyone Salutes It Day
holidays.description: This day celebrates trying out a bold, half-baked or brilliant idea on the world and seeing who rallies behind it. It's a good day to pitch that wild plan, whether it's a business idea, a new hobby or a questionable casserole.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. The name comes from a classic advertising-world phrase for testing an idea on an audience to gauge its reception.
holidays.funFact: The phrase is often linked to Madison Avenue ad culture, where executives floated concepts to see whether clients would back them.

holidays.name: Buffet Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the all-you-can-eat spread, where you can pile your plate with a bit of everything and go back for seconds. Strategy is encouraged, and so is leaving room for dessert.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It falls just after the holiday feasting season, which makes it a fitting follow-up for hearty appetites.
holidays.funFact: The word buffet comes from French, and the style of self-serve dining is often associated with Scandinavian smorgasbord traditions.
